report.title: Transfer: intelligence-community structured analytic techniques to deliberation protocols
report.question_or_target: Which structured analytic techniques - analysis of competing hypotheses, key assumptions check, devil's advocacy, team A/team B, premortem, ICD-203 analytic standards - are directly implementable as council protocol blueprints, and what does each require that a plain debate protocol does not?
report.evidence_requirement_verbatim: two mechanically independent signals per load-bearing claim (rules/common/single-signal-verification.md); every claim carries source lineage (resolved URL + fetch timestamp + sha256 of the fetched bytes), a Sherman-Kent confidence band, and a named independent verification path (_USER-PROMPTS.md:10717); each technique cites its primary methodological source (tradecraft manual or peer-reviewed evaluation) and its documented failure mode, not only its procedure
tests_required: negative control: include the published critiques of ACH (it can entrench a bad hypothesis set) so the transfer records the technique's weakness, not just its pitch
report.answer: ACH, KAC, Devil's Advocacy, Team A/Team B, and premortem are bounded session protocols that each require artifacts a plain debate does not; ICD-203 is a cross-cutting product-acceptance wrapper. Live probes bind those claims to fetched source bytes and reject a KAC claim that denies listing and review of key assumptions. Direct implementability is YES-WITH-GUARDRAILS; comparative council accuracy is unmeasured.

plain_debate_baseline.definition: A moderator gives participants turns to offer arguments and rebuttals, then the group or chair reaches a decision. Unless separately specified, there is no mandatory hypothesis, assumption, evidence, risk, or indicator register; no protected challenge role; no calibrated uncertainty rule; and no post-session evaluation loop.
plain_debate_baseline.scope_note: This is the comparison baseline defined for this transfer, not a claim that every real-world debate lacks these features.

techniques.name: Analysis of Competing Hypotheses
techniques.claim: ACH is directly implementable as an amendable council hypothesis-testing protocol; unlike plain debate it requires an explicit alternative set, an evidence-by-hypothesis matrix, diagnosticity and inconsistency judgments, sensitivity checks, and observable update indicators.
techniques.trigger: The council must compare uncertain explanations or forecasts supported by overlapping evidence.
roles: facilitator who enforces separate generation and evaluation phases
evidence steward who records provenance, credibility, and relevance
decision owner who records a provisional ranking, not a proof
ordered_steps: Frame one decision-relevant question and define the time horizon.
Independently generate alternatives before group discussion; merge them into a mutually exclusive and as-exhaustive-as-practical register.
List significant evidence, arguments, assumptions, missing evidence, source quality, and provenance.
Build the evidence-by-hypothesis matrix and judge each row against every hypothesis.
Identify diagnostic evidence; remove or down-weight evidence that does not distinguish alternatives.
Seek inconsistency and disconfirmation, then rank hypotheses provisionally by the weight of evidence against them.
Stress-test linchpin evidence and assumptions; add, split, or reopen hypotheses when the matrix exposes a bad partition.
Record rejected alternatives, uncertainty, collection gaps, and observable indicators that would change the ranking.
required_artifacts: versioned hypothesis register with an OTHER/UNKNOWN escape hatch
evidence ledger with source provenance and quality
plain_debate_delta: alternatives exist before advocacy begins
each evidence item is compared across every live hypothesis
disconfirming evidence is privileged over rhetorical support
the decision is auditable and explicitly reopenable
techniques.documented_failure_mode: The structure can entrench a bad initial hypothesis set: it evaluates what was admitted to the matrix, and repeated exposure to that list can inhibit generation of new alternatives. Published evaluations also report incomplete adherence, mixed or absent confirmation-bias reduction, inconsistent or erroneous judgments, and ranking instability.
transfer_guardrails: run independent, blind hypothesis generation before exposing the matrix
require an outsider to propose omitted alternatives and permit add/split/reframe operations throughout
treat matrix marks as structured judgments, not probabilities or mechanical truth
run a sensitivity pass and report ties, ambiguity, and an OTHER/UNKNOWN case
techniques.stop_rule: Stop only after an outsider has attempted hypothesis expansion, every decisive evidence row has provenance, and the decision owner has named evidence or indicators that would reopen the ranking.
techniques.output: A provisional, auditable hypothesis ranking plus collection and update triggers.

techniques.name: Key Assumptions Check
techniques.claim: A Key Assumptions Check is directly implementable as a council assumption-audit protocol; unlike plain debate it requires a written analytic line, an explicit stated-and-unstated assumption ledger, fragility and consequence ratings, and named indicators and review dates.
techniques.trigger: A proposed judgment or plan depends on incomplete information, inherited premises, or conditions that may change.
roles: facilitator who distinguishes evidence from assumptions
ordered_steps: Write the current analytic line or plan in one inspectable statement.
Have members silently list stated and unstated premises that must hold for that line to remain valid.
Classify each entry as evidence, assumption, uncertainty, or dependency.
Challenge why each assumption must be true, when it could fail, and whether it remains valid under all relevant conditions.
Rate evidential support, consequence if false, and sensitivity of the conclusion.
Revise the analytic line or plan, assign an owner, and name a falsifier, indicator, and review date for every linchpin assumption.
required_artifacts: owner, falsifier, indicator, and review-date register
plain_debate_delta: unstated premises become first-class review objects
fragility and consequence are rated separately from persuasiveness
assumptions remain monitored after the meeting
techniques.documented_failure_mode: A hurried or one-off KAC can merely restate shared premises and complicate the analysis; the published critical evaluation says the technique must be methodological, rigorous, and frequent and identifies time and resource pressure as a barrier.
transfer_guardrails: use silent elicitation before discussion to reduce anchoring
invite an outsider or affected stakeholder to surface premises insiders treat as facts
fail closed when a high-consequence assumption lacks an owner or falsifier
schedule repeated checks rather than treating the ledger as a one-time workshop output
techniques.stop_rule: Stop when every linchpin premise is labeled, challenged, owned, and linked to a falsifier and review date, or explicitly escalated as an unresolved uncertainty.
techniques.output: A revised analytic line and a living assumption-monitoring register.

techniques.name: Devil's Advocacy
techniques.claim: Devil's Advocacy is directly implementable as a protected council challenge protocol for one dominant view; unlike plain debate it requires a commissioned strongest countercase, protected access and airtime, a mandatory written response, and adjudication of what changed.
techniques.trigger: A strong consensus or linchpin assumption exists on a consequential question and has not faced a serious alternative case.
roles: protected challenger with the same evidence access as the main team
ordered_steps: Freeze the dominant judgment, its evidence, assumptions, and confidence before challenge.
Commission a challenger to build the strongest evidence-based alternative, not a straw person.
Give the challenger equal source access, preparation time, and uninterrupted presentation time.
Require the main team to answer each counterargument and identify evidence that would decide between positions.
Have a neutral adjudicator record retained, revised, or unresolved judgments and any new indicators or collection tasks.
Protect and separately record any authentic dissent that emerges; do not subsume it into the assigned role.
required_artifacts: commission and scope for the challenger
best countercase with evidence and falsifiers
plain_debate_delta: dissent is commissioned and protected rather than optional
the countercase must be the strongest available alternative
the dominant side owes a traceable response
the chair records whether the challenge changed the product
techniques.documented_failure_mode: Assigned dissent is not equivalent to genuine dissent: the cited experiment found authentic minority dissent superior to three devil's-advocate variants, while role-play could stimulate cognitive bolstering of the initial position rather than divergent thought.
transfer_guardrails: prefer a genuine dissenter when one exists and protect that person's status
do not let members dismiss the case merely because the role was assigned
score the countercase on evidence and discriminating tests, not rhetorical novelty
rotate challengers and require a neutral change log to prevent ritual compliance
techniques.stop_rule: Stop only after the dominant side has answered the strongest countercase and a neutral recorder has captured revisions, unresolved points, and discriminating tests.
techniques.output: A challenged judgment with a point-by-point response, decision log, and update tests.

techniques.name: Team A/Team B
techniques.claim: Team A/Team B is directly implementable for two or more already-strong competing views; unlike plain debate it requires separate teams, a common evidence packet, symmetric resources, independent products, cross-critique, and neutral synthesis without forced consensus.
techniques.trigger: Two or more consequential, strongly held interpretations already exist and ordinary discussion has produced gridlock or a lowest-common-denominator paper.
roles: two or more separately led analytic teams
ordered_steps: Define the shared question, horizon, evidence cutoff, deliverables, and scoring criteria.
Give each team the same core evidence, access rights, time, and staffing; disclose prior commitments and conflicts.
Teams independently produce their best case, explicit assumptions, disconfirmers, uncertainties, and information gaps.
Exchange products for written cross-critique and rebuttal before any joint session.
A neutral synthesis panel maps agreements, decisive disagreements, evidence gaps, and tests without averaging away differences.
The decision owner records a choice or unresolved fork and prohibits unofficial direct-to-decision-maker evidence channels.
required_artifacts: common evidence packet and provenance ledger
plain_debate_delta: analysis is developed independently before face-to-face advocacy
teams receive symmetric inputs and resources
cross-critique is written and preserved
synthesis exposes rather than suppresses substantive disagreement
techniques.documented_failure_mode: Competitive analysis can become politicized advocacy: the historical critique documents stovepiping, selective assumptions, and nominal debate turning into a campaign that bypasses or undercuts the ordinary analytic process.
transfer_guardrails: use a common evidence corpus with symmetric access and auditable provenance
select heterogeneous teams and disclose ideological or institutional commitments
ban privileged side channels to the decision owner during the exercise
use a neutral synthesis panel and preserve an OTHER/UNKNOWN option rather than forcing a binary frame
techniques.stop_rule: Stop after symmetric independent products and cross-critiques exist and a neutral panel has mapped disagreements, gaps, and decisive tests; do not stop merely because one team won the room.
techniques.output: Parallel cases, a neutral disagreement map, and a transparent decision or unresolved fork.

techniques.name: Premortem
techniques.claim: A premortem is directly implementable after a council has a provisional plan; unlike plain debate it requires a forced failure frame, silent independent cause generation, a risk-to-mitigation register, owners, and observable tripwires.
techniques.trigger: A plan is provisionally selected but still changeable, and optimism, hierarchy, or sunk effort may suppress reservations.
roles: facilitator who imposes the failure frame
participants closest to execution and affected stakeholders
risk owner for each accepted item
ordered_steps: Freeze the provisional plan, objectives, horizon, and success measures.
State that the plan has failed at the horizon; provide no cause.
Each participant silently writes plausible failure stories and causes before hearing others.
Collect ideas round-robin, cluster without debate, and preserve minority risks.
Rate controllability, evidence, likelihood range, impact, detectability, and time-to-intervene.
Convert priority risks into mitigations, small tests, kill criteria, owners, and tripwires.
Run a complementary success/preparade and outside-view pass so the negative frame is not the only frame.
required_artifacts: risk register with controllability and evidence
plain_debate_delta: failure is assumed rather than merely considered possible
risk generation occurs independently before social anchoring
identified causes must become owned mitigations or explicit acceptances
the council records early-warning tripwires
techniques.documented_failure_mode: Premortems do not automatically identify the most actionable risks. A published three-study critique found systematic attribution bias toward factors outside participants' control; the peer-reviewed implementation study also did not establish comparative or downstream outcome effectiveness.
transfer_guardrails: classify each risk by controllability and require at least one within-control counterpart
pair the failure frame with a success/preparade and reference-class pass
distinguish generated plausibility from likelihood and validate important risks with data or small tests
discard or explicitly accept risks that cannot change the plan rather than accumulating an ornamental list
techniques.stop_rule: Stop when every priority failure story is either linked to evidence and an owned mitigation/test or explicitly accepted, and the complementary success and outside-view passes are complete.
techniques.output: An actionable risk register with tests, mitigations, owners, kill criteria, and tripwires.

techniques.name: ICD-203 Analytic Standards
techniques.protocol_type: cross-cutting product acceptance and evaluation gate
techniques.claim: ICD-203 is directly implementable as a cross-cutting council product-acceptance wrapper, not as a standalone debate; it requires source-quality disclosure, calibrated uncertainty, evidence-assumption separation, alternatives, logical argument, change tracking, accuracy review, training, and independent product evaluation.
techniques.trigger: Every council product before release and periodically after outcomes or important new information become available.
ordered_steps: Check objectivity, political independence, timeliness, and use of available sources appropriate to the product.
Describe source quality and credibility and cite the information supporting major judgments.
Express likelihood and confidence separately and explain their evidential basis and information gaps.
Distinguish information from assumptions and judgments, and incorporate relevant alternatives and indicators.
Check customer relevance, implications, logical argument, consistency, and change from prior judgments.
Release only with an evaluation record, then backtest accuracy and calibration when outcomes mature.
Feed aggregate evaluation results into training, process repair, and protected ombuds escalation.
plain_debate_delta: the output must satisfy explicit quality and integrity criteria
uncertainty and source quality are disclosed in a standard form
independent evaluation and protected escalation exist
quality is monitored after publication rather than inferred from a persuasive meeting
techniques.documented_failure_mode: Checklist compliance can emphasize report attributes that are weak proxies for overall quality or accuracy. Official evaluation also found training and review gaps that risk inconsistent application, so a standards document alone does not operationalize itself.
transfer_guardrails: translate each standard into observable rubric items with examples and reviewer calibration
use collective or independent review rather than analyst self-certification alone
separate tradecraft compliance from outcome accuracy and maintain both scorecards
resource recurrent training, evaluation, and a protected escalation path
techniques.stop_rule: Stop only when the product passes an independent rubric review and has a scheduled outcome or calibration review; a completed checklist without evaluator agreement is not sufficient.
techniques.output: A release decision, traceable quality record, and later accuracy/calibration feedback.

Use premortem only after a provisional plan exists.
Wrap every released product in the ICD-203-derived acceptance, evaluation, and feedback gate.

title: Transfer: intelligence-community structured analytic techniques to deliberation protocols
question_or_target: Which structured analytic techniques - analysis of competing hypotheses, key assumptions check, devil's advocacy, team A/team B, premortem, ICD-203 analytic standards - are directly implementable as council protocol blueprints, and what does each require that a plain debate protocol does not?
evidence_requirement_verbatim: two mechanically independent signals per load-bearing claim (rules/common/single-signal-verification.md); every claim carries source lineage (resolved URL + fetch timestamp + sha256 of the fetched bytes), a Sherman-Kent confidence band, and a named independent verification path (_USER-PROMPTS.md:10717); each technique cites its primary methodological source (tradecraft manual or peer-reviewed evaluation) and its documented failure mode, not only its procedure
tests_required: negative control: include the published critiques of ACH (it can entrench a bad hypothesis set) so the transfer records the technique's weakness, not just its pitch
answer: ACH, KAC, Devil's Advocacy, Team A/Team B, and premortem are bounded session protocols that each require artifacts a plain debate does not; ICD-203 is a cross-cutting product-acceptance wrapper. Live probes bind those claims to fetched source bytes and reject a KAC claim that denies listing and review of key assumptions. Direct implementability is YES-WITH-GUARDRAILS; comparative council accuracy is unmeasured.

plain_debate_baseline.definition: A moderator gives participants turns to offer arguments and rebuttals, then the group or chair reaches a decision. Unless separately specified, there is no mandatory hypothesis, assumption, evidence, risk, or indicator register; no protected challenge role; no calibrated uncertainty rule; and no post-session evaluation loop.
plain_debate_baseline.scope_note: This is the comparison baseline defined for this transfer, not a claim that every real-world debate lacks these features.

techniques.name: Analysis of Competing Hypotheses
techniques.claim: ACH is directly implementable as an amendable council hypothesis-testing protocol; unlike plain debate it requires an explicit alternative set, an evidence-by-hypothesis matrix, diagnosticity and inconsistency judgments, sensitivity checks, and observable update indicators.
techniques.trigger: The council must compare uncertain explanations or forecasts supported by overlapping evidence.
roles: facilitator who enforces separate generation and evaluation phases
evidence steward who records provenance, credibility, and relevance
decision owner who records a provisional ranking, not a proof
ordered_steps: Frame one decision-relevant question and define the time horizon.
Independently generate alternatives before group discussion; merge them into a mutually exclusive and as-exhaustive-as-practical register.
List significant evidence, arguments, assumptions, missing evidence, source quality, and provenance.
Build the evidence-by-hypothesis matrix and judge each row against every hypothesis.
Identify diagnostic evidence; remove or down-weight evidence that does not distinguish alternatives.
Seek inconsistency and disconfirmation, then rank hypotheses provisionally by the weight of evidence against them.
Stress-test linchpin evidence and assumptions; add, split, or reopen hypotheses when the matrix exposes a bad partition.
Record rejected alternatives, uncertainty, collection gaps, and observable indicators that would change the ranking.
required_artifacts: versioned hypothesis register with an OTHER/UNKNOWN escape hatch
evidence ledger with source provenance and quality
plain_debate_delta: alternatives exist before advocacy begins
each evidence item is compared across every live hypothesis
disconfirming evidence is privileged over rhetorical support
the decision is auditable and explicitly reopenable
techniques.documented_failure_mode: The structure can entrench a bad initial hypothesis set: it evaluates what was admitted to the matrix, and repeated exposure to that list can inhibit generation of new alternatives. Published evaluations also report incomplete adherence, mixed or absent confirmation-bias reduction, inconsistent or erroneous judgments, and ranking instability.
transfer_guardrails: run independent, blind hypothesis generation before exposing the matrix
require an outsider to propose omitted alternatives and permit add/split/reframe operations throughout
treat matrix marks as structured judgments, not probabilities or mechanical truth
run a sensitivity pass and report ties, ambiguity, and an OTHER/UNKNOWN case
techniques.stop_rule: Stop only after an outsider has attempted hypothesis expansion, every decisive evidence row has provenance, and the decision owner has named evidence or indicators that would reopen the ranking.
techniques.output: A provisional, auditable hypothesis ranking plus collection and update triggers.

techniques.name: Key Assumptions Check
techniques.claim: A Key Assumptions Check is directly implementable as a council assumption-audit protocol; unlike plain debate it requires a written analytic line, an explicit stated-and-unstated assumption ledger, fragility and consequence ratings, and named indicators and review dates.
techniques.trigger: A proposed judgment or plan depends on incomplete information, inherited premises, or conditions that may change.
roles: facilitator who distinguishes evidence from assumptions
ordered_steps: Write the current analytic line or plan in one inspectable statement.
Have members silently list stated and unstated premises that must hold for that line to remain valid.
Classify each entry as evidence, assumption, uncertainty, or dependency.
Challenge why each assumption must be true, when it could fail, and whether it remains valid under all relevant conditions.
Rate evidential support, consequence if false, and sensitivity of the conclusion.
Revise the analytic line or plan, assign an owner, and name a falsifier, indicator, and review date for every linchpin assumption.
required_artifacts: owner, falsifier, indicator, and review-date register
plain_debate_delta: unstated premises become first-class review objects
fragility and consequence are rated separately from persuasiveness
assumptions remain monitored after the meeting
techniques.documented_failure_mode: A hurried or one-off KAC can merely restate shared premises and complicate the analysis; the published critical evaluation says the technique must be methodological, rigorous, and frequent and identifies time and resource pressure as a barrier.
transfer_guardrails: use silent elicitation before discussion to reduce anchoring
invite an outsider or affected stakeholder to surface premises insiders treat as facts
fail closed when a high-consequence assumption lacks an owner or falsifier
schedule repeated checks rather than treating the ledger as a one-time workshop output
techniques.stop_rule: Stop when every linchpin premise is labeled, challenged, owned, and linked to a falsifier and review date, or explicitly escalated as an unresolved uncertainty.
techniques.output: A revised analytic line and a living assumption-monitoring register.

techniques.name: Devil's Advocacy
techniques.claim: Devil's Advocacy is directly implementable as a protected council challenge protocol for one dominant view; unlike plain debate it requires a commissioned strongest countercase, protected access and airtime, a mandatory written response, and adjudication of what changed.
techniques.trigger: A strong consensus or linchpin assumption exists on a consequential question and has not faced a serious alternative case.
roles: protected challenger with the same evidence access as the main team
ordered_steps: Freeze the dominant judgment, its evidence, assumptions, and confidence before challenge.
Commission a challenger to build the strongest evidence-based alternative, not a straw person.
Give the challenger equal source access, preparation time, and uninterrupted presentation time.
Require the main team to answer each counterargument and identify evidence that would decide between positions.
Have a neutral adjudicator record retained, revised, or unresolved judgments and any new indicators or collection tasks.
Protect and separately record any authentic dissent that emerges; do not subsume it into the assigned role.
required_artifacts: commission and scope for the challenger
best countercase with evidence and falsifiers
plain_debate_delta: dissent is commissioned and protected rather than optional
the countercase must be the strongest available alternative
the dominant side owes a traceable response
the chair records whether the challenge changed the product
techniques.documented_failure_mode: Assigned dissent is not equivalent to genuine dissent: the cited experiment found authentic minority dissent superior to three devil's-advocate variants, while role-play could stimulate cognitive bolstering of the initial position rather than divergent thought.
transfer_guardrails: prefer a genuine dissenter when one exists and protect that person's status
do not let members dismiss the case merely because the role was assigned
score the countercase on evidence and discriminating tests, not rhetorical novelty
rotate challengers and require a neutral change log to prevent ritual compliance
techniques.stop_rule: Stop only after the dominant side has answered the strongest countercase and a neutral recorder has captured revisions, unresolved points, and discriminating tests.
techniques.output: A challenged judgment with a point-by-point response, decision log, and update tests.

techniques.name: Team A/Team B
techniques.claim: Team A/Team B is directly implementable for two or more already-strong competing views; unlike plain debate it requires separate teams, a common evidence packet, symmetric resources, independent products, cross-critique, and neutral synthesis without forced consensus.
techniques.trigger: Two or more consequential, strongly held interpretations already exist and ordinary discussion has produced gridlock or a lowest-common-denominator paper.
roles: two or more separately led analytic teams
ordered_steps: Define the shared question, horizon, evidence cutoff, deliverables, and scoring criteria.
Give each team the same core evidence, access rights, time, and staffing; disclose prior commitments and conflicts.
Teams independently produce their best case, explicit assumptions, disconfirmers, uncertainties, and information gaps.
Exchange products for written cross-critique and rebuttal before any joint session.
A neutral synthesis panel maps agreements, decisive disagreements, evidence gaps, and tests without averaging away differences.
The decision owner records a choice or unresolved fork and prohibits unofficial direct-to-decision-maker evidence channels.
required_artifacts: common evidence packet and provenance ledger
plain_debate_delta: analysis is developed independently before face-to-face advocacy
teams receive symmetric inputs and resources
cross-critique is written and preserved
synthesis exposes rather than suppresses substantive disagreement
techniques.documented_failure_mode: Competitive analysis can become politicized advocacy: the historical critique documents stovepiping, selective assumptions, and nominal debate turning into a campaign that bypasses or undercuts the ordinary analytic process.
transfer_guardrails: use a common evidence corpus with symmetric access and auditable provenance
select heterogeneous teams and disclose ideological or institutional commitments
ban privileged side channels to the decision owner during the exercise
use a neutral synthesis panel and preserve an OTHER/UNKNOWN option rather than forcing a binary frame
techniques.stop_rule: Stop after symmetric independent products and cross-critiques exist and a neutral panel has mapped disagreements, gaps, and decisive tests; do not stop merely because one team won the room.
techniques.output: Parallel cases, a neutral disagreement map, and a transparent decision or unresolved fork.

techniques.name: Premortem
techniques.claim: A premortem is directly implementable after a council has a provisional plan; unlike plain debate it requires a forced failure frame, silent independent cause generation, a risk-to-mitigation register, owners, and observable tripwires.
techniques.trigger: A plan is provisionally selected but still changeable, and optimism, hierarchy, or sunk effort may suppress reservations.
roles: facilitator who imposes the failure frame
participants closest to execution and affected stakeholders
risk owner for each accepted item
ordered_steps: Freeze the provisional plan, objectives, horizon, and success measures.
State that the plan has failed at the horizon; provide no cause.
Each participant silently writes plausible failure stories and causes before hearing others.
Collect ideas round-robin, cluster without debate, and preserve minority risks.
Rate controllability, evidence, likelihood range, impact, detectability, and time-to-intervene.
Convert priority risks into mitigations, small tests, kill criteria, owners, and tripwires.
Run a complementary success/preparade and outside-view pass so the negative frame is not the only frame.
required_artifacts: risk register with controllability and evidence
plain_debate_delta: failure is assumed rather than merely considered possible
risk generation occurs independently before social anchoring
identified causes must become owned mitigations or explicit acceptances
the council records early-warning tripwires
techniques.documented_failure_mode: Premortems do not automatically identify the most actionable risks. A published three-study critique found systematic attribution bias toward factors outside participants' control; the peer-reviewed implementation study also did not establish comparative or downstream outcome effectiveness.
transfer_guardrails: classify each risk by controllability and require at least one within-control counterpart
pair the failure frame with a success/preparade and reference-class pass
distinguish generated plausibility from likelihood and validate important risks with data or small tests
discard or explicitly accept risks that cannot change the plan rather than accumulating an ornamental list
techniques.stop_rule: Stop when every priority failure story is either linked to evidence and an owned mitigation/test or explicitly accepted, and the complementary success and outside-view passes are complete.
techniques.output: An actionable risk register with tests, mitigations, owners, kill criteria, and tripwires.

techniques.name: ICD-203 Analytic Standards
techniques.protocol_type: cross-cutting product acceptance and evaluation gate
techniques.claim: ICD-203 is directly implementable as a cross-cutting council product-acceptance wrapper, not as a standalone debate; it requires source-quality disclosure, calibrated uncertainty, evidence-assumption separation, alternatives, logical argument, change tracking, accuracy review, training, and independent product evaluation.
techniques.trigger: Every council product before release and periodically after outcomes or important new information become available.
ordered_steps: Check objectivity, political independence, timeliness, and use of available sources appropriate to the product.
Describe source quality and credibility and cite the information supporting major judgments.
Express likelihood and confidence separately and explain their evidential basis and information gaps.
Distinguish information from assumptions and judgments, and incorporate relevant alternatives and indicators.
Check customer relevance, implications, logical argument, consistency, and change from prior judgments.
Release only with an evaluation record, then backtest accuracy and calibration when outcomes mature.
Feed aggregate evaluation results into training, process repair, and protected ombuds escalation.
plain_debate_delta: the output must satisfy explicit quality and integrity criteria
uncertainty and source quality are disclosed in a standard form
independent evaluation and protected escalation exist
quality is monitored after publication rather than inferred from a persuasive meeting
techniques.documented_failure_mode: Checklist compliance can emphasize report attributes that are weak proxies for overall quality or accuracy. Official evaluation also found training and review gaps that risk inconsistent application, so a standards document alone does not operationalize itself.
transfer_guardrails: translate each standard into observable rubric items with examples and reviewer calibration
use collective or independent review rather than analyst self-certification alone
separate tradecraft compliance from outcome accuracy and maintain both scorecards
resource recurrent training, evaluation, and a protected escalation path
techniques.stop_rule: Stop only when the product passes an independent rubric review and has a scheduled outcome or calibration review; a completed checklist without evaluator agreement is not sufficient.
techniques.output: A release decision, traceable quality record, and later accuracy/calibration feedback.

synthesis.claim: All six are implementable as council blueprints, but none is merely 'better debate': ACH, KAC, Devil's Advocacy, Team A/Team B, and premortem are bounded session protocols, while ICD-203 is a cross-cutting acceptance and learning wrapper. Each adds persistent state, specialized roles, mandatory artifacts, and a stop or update rule that the defined plain-debate baseline lacks.
implementation_order: Use KAC at framing to surface premises.
Use ACH when the decision turns on competing explanations.
Use Devil's Advocacy for one dominant consensus or Team A/Team B for multiple entrenched views; do not confuse their triggers.
Use premortem only after a provisional plan exists.
Wrap every released product in the ICD-203-derived acceptance, evaluation, and feedback gate.
